title: Gamifying Clinical Breathing Training
subtitle: A heart rate variability biofeedback game, and what gamification costs

slides.title: Gamifying Clinical Breathing Training
slides.standfirst: An Android flight game that turns resonant frequency breathing into something playable — and a controlled study measuring what that fun actually costs in clinical performance terms.

bullets.text: UX Researcher and Co-Designer
11 participants aged 40 to 67, three game modes
The mode that motivated players most was not the mode they breathed best in

slides.notes: Lead with the counter-intuitive finding on the cover. It is the reason this study is worth a paper rather than a demo.

slides.title: Why breathing at your resonant frequency raises HRV
slides.standfirst: Reduced heart rate variability indicates a malfunctioning autonomic nervous system — and can be either the cause or the consequence of disease.
slides.notes: Two minutes of physiology here earns the rest of the deck. Without it, the game looks like a toy.

slides.title: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia
slides.standfirst: Heart rate rises on the in-breath and falls on the out-breath. Breathe at roughly six breaths a minute and that oscillation goes into resonance, producing large, coherent swings in heart rate.

bullets.text: Resonant frequency breathing is a viable non-invasive intervention for rebalancing the autonomic nervous system.
It raises HRV without medication, equipment implants, or a clinician in the room.
The exercises are widely regarded as boring and monotonous, which undermines adherence.

slides.title: Six breaths a minute, live
slides.standfirst: Ten seconds a cycle. Follow the pacer and watch heart rate track it — that phase lock is the whole intervention.

figure.caption: Resonant-frequency pacer with the coupled heart-rate wave

slides.notes: Invite the audience to breathe with it. Thirty seconds of the room doing this together makes the boredom problem self-evident — which is exactly the setup for the game.

slides.title: Real signal, not a simulated one
slides.standfirst: Heart rate came off an ECG device, so the biofeedback loop closed on actual interbeat intervals rather than on a proxy.

bullets.text: Interbeat intervals streamed to the Android device in real time.
The game's biofeedback framework converted the HRV signal into game state.
Which means training performance was measurable, per participant, per mode.

slides.notes: Worth stressing: measurable performance is what allows the motivation-versus-performance split later. A game with fake feedback cannot produce that finding.

slides.title: Gamification raises motivation. Nobody had measured what it does to the training.

bullets.text: Gamification is a recognised route to higher motivation and engagement.
How to design a game for breathing exercises specifically.
How additional interactive elements affect the main course of training.

callout.text: Adding fun could improve adherence while degrading the clinical activity it exists to support. You would ship more sessions of worse training and call it a win.

slides.notes: This is the thesis. Everything after it is method built to test this one sentence.

slides.title: A full user-centred process, not a jump to implementation
slides.notes: Say this because the temptation in a games project is always to start building. The concept-selection stage is what kept the study honest.

slides.title: Five candidate concepts, generated after analysing what already existed
slides.standfirst: Context analysis of breathing applications on the Google Play Store first, then five distinct game principles — each demanding a different kind of attention.

figure.caption: Five game principles, narrowed by survey rather than by taste

slides.notes: Point out that these vary deliberately in attentional load — that variation is the independent variable the whole study rests on.

slides.title: GameFlow, then icons tested for both directions of association
slides.standfirst: Before any code, the mockups were evaluated against the GameFlow model with 10 different participants — and every icon had to earn its place.

slides.notes: The scoreboard and statistics screens are the adherence machinery. The flight scene is where the clinical activity actually happens.

slides.title: Three modes, varying only in how much multitasking they demand
slides.standfirst: This is the design of the study, not a feature list. Holding everything else constant is what allows motivation gains and clinical losses to be attributed rather than confounded.

slides.title: The curves diverge
slides.standfirst: Video games do motivate HRV biofeedback training — and the motivating mode was not the effective one.

bullets.text: The highest training performance on first attempt came from pure visualisation, not from any multitasking mode.
Players were more motivated by the more challenging game.
And more interested in long-term engagement with it.

callout.lead: So the honest conclusion is not "gamify" or "don't"
callout.text: Multitasking has considerable influence on HRV biofeedback and should be deployed with an adaptive challenge level — meeting the clinical requirement early and the motivational one over time.

slides.notes: Do not soften this. A study that had found gamification straightforwardly good would have been less useful and less believable.

slides.title: A reusable framework, published
slides.standfirst: The contribution is not the game. It is a documented method for designing and evaluating gamified HRV biofeedback, in a space that had almost none.

slides.notes: Three modes is the number that matters. It is the difference between a game and an experiment.

slides.title: Engagement and efficacy are separate variables, and they can move in opposite directions
slides.standfirst: In any therapeutic product, every element added to hold attention competes for the attention the therapy requires. If you only measure engagement, you will never see the trade.

callout.lead: Which is why the recommendation is adaptive
callout.text: Start where the clinical performance is, and add challenge as competence grows. One fixed difficulty has to sacrifice either the first session or the fiftieth.

slides.notes: This generalises well beyond breathing training — meditation, physio, adherence apps. Make that link if the audience is a product one.
